attrs.management_says: Operating cash flow increase due to 'changes in working capital and higher non-cash expenses such as stock-based compensation and restructuring and other charges... partially offset by a decline in net income.'
attrs.numbers_show: CFO rose $269M (29.7%) while net income fell $17M. Inventory provisions increased $53M (from $59M to $112M). SG&A rose $121M (25%), likely including stock-based compensation. Quarterly DSO improvement in H2 released cash. Depreciation fell $19M, so non-cash boost came from other sources.

attrs.reason: CFO rose $269M while net income fell $17M. Inventory provisions increased $53M (E43), a visible non-cash charge supporting part of the explanation. However, the other cited non-cash drivers—stock-based compensation and restructuring—are not broken out in the pack; the $121M SG&A increase (E3→E15) includes both cash and non-cash items with no FY2016 disclosure. Working capital changes are not fully visible: year-over-year receivables rose $31.4M (use of cash), and inventory/payables details are absent. Quarterly DSO improvement in H2 (E29, E30) suggests some cash release, but the net working capital impact cannot be quantified. The explanation therefore relies on management's word for the magnitude and composition of non-cash expenses and working capital shifts.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: Operating cash flow increased $269M despite a $17M net income decline because inventory provisions rose $53M (from $59M to $112M), SG&A increased $121M (likely including stock-based compensation), and DSO improved sharply in H2 (from 42 to 37 days in Q3 and 34 to 33 days in Q4), releasing cash from working capital.
